pattern_name: Spontaneous fluency, paraphrase and seamless repair
pattern_name_ar: الطلاقة العفوية وإعادة الصياغة والتصحيح السلس
formula: Real fillers: well, I mean, the thing is, let me put it this way · Reformulation: or rather, to put it more precisely, what I should say is · Inline repair: — Wednesday, sorry — · Time-buying: let me separate two things, before I answer that
formula_visual: [It was unsuccessful] — [or rather], [it was never properly tried]
when_to_use: In any unscripted speech: interviews, meetings, seminars, negotiations. Fluent speakers hesitate constantly, but they hesitate with language rather than with 'erm'. They also refine formulations mid-sentence and repair genuine slips without stopping. These devices are what make unprepared speech sound composed.
when_to_use_ar: في أي كلام غير مُعدّ: المقابلات والاجتماعات والحلقات والمفاوضات. المتحدّث الطليق يتردّد كثيرًا لكنه يتردّد بلغة لا بـ 'erm'. ويصقل الصياغة أثناء الجملة ويصحّح الزلّات دون توقّف.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Learners are often taught that hesitation is a defect to be eliminated, so when it inevitably occurs they treat it as failure: they stop, apologise, or restart the sentence, all of which cost far more credibility than the original hesitation would have. Arabic has its own repair and floor-holding formulae, but they do not transfer, leaving a gap that gets filled with 'erm' and with silence that invites interruption.

examples.en: Well, the thing is, nobody actually asked.
examples.ar: في الحقيقة، لم يسأل أحد فعلًا

examples.en: It was unsuccessful — or rather, it was never properly tried.
examples.ar: لم ينجح، أو بالأحرى لم يُجرَّب فعلًا

examples.en: We met on Tuesday — Wednesday, sorry — and agreed the terms.
examples.ar: اجتمعنا الثلاثاء — الأربعاء، عفوًا — واتّفقنا على الشروط

examples.en: That is a good question, and I want to answer it properly.
examples.ar: سؤال جيد، وأريد أن أجيب عنه كما ينبغي

examples.en: Let me separate two things, because they are being confused.
examples.ar: دعني أفصل بين أمرين لأنهما يُخلطان

common_errors.wrong: Sorry, sorry, let me start that sentence again from the beginning.
common_errors.correct: It was unsuccessful — or rather, it was never properly tried.
common_errors.explanation: Repair inside the sentence and continue; restarting costs more than the slip.

common_errors.wrong: Erm... erm... how do you say... erm...
common_errors.correct: Let me put it this way. / The thing is, …
common_errors.explanation: A real phrase occupies the same time but signals control rather than difficulty.

common_errors.wrong: I don't know. (falling tone, then silence)
common_errors.correct: It depends, really, on what you mean by that.
common_errors.explanation: A falling tone plus silence hands your turn to someone else before you have finished.

common_errors.wrong: It was unsuccessful. Sorry, that's wrong. It was never tried.
common_errors.correct: It was unsuccessful — or rather, it was never properly tried.
common_errors.explanation: Reformulate in the same breath; announcing the correction breaks the flow unnecessarily.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: Well, the ___ is, nobody actually asked.
It was unsuccessful — or ___, it was never properly tried.
We met on Tuesday — Wednesday, ___ — and agreed the terms.
That is a good question, and I want to answer it ___.
Let me ___ two things, because they are being confused.

quick_rule: Hesitate in ENGLISH, not with 'erm'. Reformulate with 'or rather' at the same pace. Repair inline and continue. Never apologise or restart.
quick_rule_ar: تردّد بالإنجليزية لا بـ 'erm'. وأعد الصياغة بـ 'or rather' بالسرعة نفسها. وصحّح داخل الجريان وتابع. ولا تعتذر ولا تُعِد من البداية.
mnemonic: Repair, don't restart. Hold, don't fill.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 19 you drilled level-tone pauses that hold your turn and reformulations delivered at unchanged pace. A falling pause invites interruption, so the tone of your hesitation matters as much as its content.
